USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: We should hold our current tariff leverage and pivot back to negotiation rather than escalate further. The US has already deployed maximum coverage (25% on ~$250B plus the Aug 1 announcement of 10% on the remaining ~$300B effective Sept 1, and the Aug 5 currency-manipulator designation), so additional escalation now would only raise consumer prices on apparel/electronics, deepen recession risk, and invite more Chinese retaliation (suspended agricultural purchases, yuan depreciation, rare-earth threats) with no prospect of a matching concession. Keep existing tariffs as bargaining leverage but refrain from pulling the Sept 1 consumer-goods trigger and signal readiness to resume serious talks.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high (+0.45), just below the +0.5 'material GDP drag / key export sector exposed / mounting domestic political pressure' anchor. The escalation is now demonstrably biting US markets and the real economy: University of Michigan consumer sentiment plunged to 89.8 in August from 98.4 in July, the 10-year Treasury fell to 1.71% (from ~2.65 in February), and the 3M-10Y curve inverted, with the Dow posting its worst day of 2019 on Aug 5 (CNBC/CNN). The new $300B tranche hits consumer goods directly — 42% of US apparel and 69% of footwear come from China — and US agriculture is exposed, with China suspending purchases of a ~$9B/yr market (American Farm Bureau). China has not conceded: it retaliated by suspending US ag purchases (CNBC, Aug 5) and letting the yuan break 7, prompting the Treasury's currency-manipulator designation (timeline Aug 5), and it retains rare-earth leverage critical to US defense (CRS). Action stance is mild de-escalation-to-negotiate (+0.1) precisely because the high threat argues against further escalation: our leverage is already at its ceiling, the Fed has only just cut for the first time in 11 years (fed funds to 2.13), and the on-again/off-again pattern is destroying business confidence. Escalating further risks a self-inflicted recession, while unilateral concession is premature absent a matching Chinese offer — so the disciplined course is to preserve bargaining position, delay the self-damaging Sept 1 consumer tariff, and return to the table.

CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold our current posture — stand firm on the yuan-break-7 and halted farm purchases, keep the Shanghai/OECD negotiating channel open, and hold the rare-earth and Unreliable Entities List tools in reserve rather than activate broad new escalation. Avoid escalating into a full currency/tariff spiral that would damage our own slowing export economy more than it pressures Washington, but make no one-sided concessions while the US has offered no matching rollback.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high but not existential. The US imposed 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4, effective Sept 1) on 2019-08-01, which combined with the 25% on $250B would cover essentially our entire export base to the US, and on 2019-08-05 designated China a currency manipulator as CNY broke 7 for the first time since 2008 — material FX and capital-outflow pressure against the CHN high anchor (export sectors hit, firm-level Huawei targeting). Firm-level targeting is real: Huawei's entity-listing (May 16) cut projected revenue to $100B from $120B with Android/GMS access suspended, threatening tech self-sufficiency goals. Against this, the situation is not existential: Beijing has real counter-leverage (rare-earth signal from Xi's Jiangxi visit; Unreliable Entities List; halting US farm purchases directly hits Trump's rural base), the yuan depreciation itself cushions the tariff drag, and the US shows clear strain — 10Y Treasuries collapsed to 1.71% and 2Y to 1.59%, consumer sentiment crashed to 89.8 in August, and the Fed cut to 2.13% — showing the trade war is biting Washington and giving us negotiating leverage. Hence action is firmly held (score near zero): further escalation would cut our own exports and deter foreign investment (EU Chamber warns the list could hurt China's own interests) more than it helps, while concession without US reciprocity is politically and economically unjustified. Hold and keep talking.
